primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Behçet syndrome is a systemic autoinflammatory vasculitis capable of involving arteries and veins of variable caliber. Active lesions commonly show neutrophil-predominant vascular inflammation and thrombosis; the same inflammatory disease produces recurrent oral and genital aphthae, uveitis, pathergy, and arterial or venous vascular lesions.
vignette: A 29-year-old man has recurrent painful oral ulcers, recurrent scrotal ulcers that heal with scars, and two episodes of anterior uveitis. Twenty-four hours after venipuncture, a sterile erythematous pustule develops at the needle site. He now has unilateral calf swelling, and ultrasonography confirms a deep venous thrombosis.
lead: Which vascular pathologic pattern best fits the underlying disorder in this patient?
correct: Neutrophil-predominant vasculitis with thrombosis that can involve both arteries and veins of variable caliber
distractors: Granulomatous arteritis with multinucleated giant cells involving medium and large arteries
IgA-dominant immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis with palpable purpura and glomerulonephritis
Necrotizing granulomatous inflammation centered on the upper and lower respiratory tract with pauci-immune glomerulonephritis
Eosinophil-rich necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis associated with asthma and peripheral eosinophilia
distractor_notes: Granulomatous inflammation with giant cells in medium and large arteries describes giant cell arteritis. Behçet syndrome is a variable-vessel disease involving both arteries and veins and does not require giant-cell granulomatous pathology.

IgA vasculitis is an immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis that classically causes palpable purpura and can involve the kidneys, joints, and gastrointestinal tract. It does not explain the recurrent oral/genital aphthae, uveitis, pathergy, and variable-vessel thrombosis pattern.
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis classically combines necrotizing granulomatous respiratory disease with pauci-immune glomerulonephritis; those findings are absent here.

Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis is associated with asthma, eosinophilia, and eosinophil-rich necrotizing granulomatous inflammation rather than the Behçet mucocutaneous-ocular-pathergy syndrome.
key_expl: Recurrent oral aphthae, scar-forming genital ulcers, uveitis, a positive pathergy reaction, and venous thrombosis identify Behçet syndrome. Behçet is unusual among vasculitides because it can affect both arteries and veins of all sizes. Histopathology commonly shows vascular inflammation with a prominent neutrophilic reaction and thrombosis. Venous thrombosis is a well-recognized vascular manifestation, while arterial disease can produce occlusions or aneurysms, including pulmonary artery aneurysms.
objective: Recognize Behçet syndrome as a variable-vessel systemic vasculitis affecting both arteries and veins, with neutrophilic vascular inflammation and thrombosis accompanying recurrent aphthous, ocular, and pathergy manifestations.
